checks.question: Are caught errors ignored, logged without action, or replaced with null/empty/default values, silently swallowing failures (swallowed exception/error)? (ERR-001)

onYes.title: Fix swallowed errors (ERR-001): handle, propagate, or log with context
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Swallowed exceptions hide failures, producing silent data loss and undebuggable behavior.

Find all instances: Search for empty catch blocks, catches that only log and continue inappropriately, and error handlers that substitute null/empty/default while the operation actually failed.

Fix correctly: Handle the error meaningfully, propagate it, or log with enough context AND preserve failure semantics (don't pretend success). Only suppress an error when there is a deliberate, documented reason.

Constraints: Do not weaken behavior to make code 'not throw'. Preserve failure state.

Acceptance: Errors are handled or propagated, not silently dropped. Add a test asserting the failure surfaces (exception/result) rather than a fake success.

checks.question: Are broad catch-all blocks handling unrelated failures identically without classifying by type/recoverability (catch-all without classification)? (ERR-002)

onYes.title: Fix catch-all without classification (ERR-002): catch specific failures
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Catching everything the same way masks bugs (e.g. treating a programming error like a transient network blip).

Find all instances: Search for broad catches (catch Exception/Throwable/catch-all) that handle distinct failures identically.

Fix correctly: Catch specific exception types and branch by recoverability (retryable vs permanent vs programmer error). Let truly unexpected errors propagate.

Constraints: Don't catch errors you can't handle. Preserve stack/cause when rethrowing.

Acceptance: Error handling distinguishes failure categories. Add tests asserting different failure types take the correct branch.

checks.question: Do error paths return success status, empty results, default data, or completed tasks/promises, converting a failure into a silent success? (ERR-003)

onYes.title: Fix failure-as-success (ERR-003): preserve failure state
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Returning success on failure corrupts downstream logic and hides outages.

Find all instances: Search error branches that return OK/empty/default or resolve a task as if successful.

Fix correctly: Preserve and surface failure state (error result/exception/appropriate status). Expose partial-success explicitly where relevant.

Constraints: Don't fabricate data on failure. Map to correct status codes (API-007).

Acceptance: Failures are reported, not disguised. Add a test asserting a failed operation returns a failure, not success.

checks.question: Are resources, locks, transactions, files, temp state, or metrics not cleaned up when errors occur (missing cleanup on failure)? (ERR-004)

onYes.title: Fix missing cleanup on failure (ERR-004): use finally/scope guards
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Leaking resources/locks on the error path causes exhaustion, deadlocks, and corruption.

Find all instances: Search error paths for resources/locks/transactions/files/temp state acquired but not released when exceptions occur.

Fix correctly: Use finally/using/defer/scope guards or transactions so cleanup runs on every path. Roll back transactions on failure.

Constraints: Ensure cleanup itself can't mask the original error.

Acceptance: Cleanup runs on success and failure. Add a test that forces an error mid-operation and asserts resources are released/rolled back.

checks.question: Are retries applied around validation failures, auth failures, permanent errors, duplicate requests, or malformed input (retrying non-retryable failure)? (ERR-005)

onYes.title: Fix retrying non-retryable failures (ERR-005): retry only transient errors
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Retrying permanent failures wastes resources and can cause duplicate side effects.

Find all instances: Search retry logic that wraps validation/auth/4xx/permanent errors.

Fix correctly: Classify failures and retry only transient ones (timeouts, 5xx, connection resets). Fail fast on permanent errors.

Constraints: Combine with idempotency (CON-016) to make any retry safe.

Acceptance: Only transient failures are retried. Add tests asserting permanent failures are not retried and transient ones are.

checks.question: Do calls to external dependencies fail immediately on transient errors with no retry/backoff policy (missing retry/backoff for transient failure)? (ERR-006)

onYes.title: Fix missing retry/backoff (ERR-006): add bounded backoff with jitter
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Without retries, brief transient failures cause unnecessary user-visible errors.

Find all instances: Search external dependency calls (HTTP/DB/queue/RPC) that surface transient failures without any retry policy.

Fix correctly: Add bounded exponential backoff with jitter and deadline awareness for transient failures only, ensuring the operation is idempotent or guarded.

Constraints: Bound attempts and total time (ERR-007). Retry only transient errors (ERR-005).

Acceptance: Transient failures are retried with bounded backoff. Add a test asserting a transient failure is retried and eventually succeeds/fails within bounds.

checks.question: Are there retry loops without a max-attempt cap, total deadline, cancellation, or escalation (unbounded retry loop)? (ERR-007)

onYes.title: Fix unbounded retry loop (ERR-007): cap attempts and deadlines
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Unbounded retries can hammer dependencies, hang requests, and amplify outages.

Find all instances: Search retry loops lacking max attempts, total deadline, cancellation handling, or fail-fast escalation.

Fix correctly: Add max attempts, an overall deadline, jitter, cancellation support, and escalation/fail-fast when exhausted.

Constraints: Respect upstream deadlines (ERR-009). Config over hardcoding for limits.

Acceptance: Retries are bounded and cancellable. Add a test asserting the loop stops after max attempts/deadline.

checks.question: Are network, database, subprocess, queue, RPC, or file operations issued without an explicit timeout, allowing indefinite blocking (missing timeout on external call)? (ERR-008)

onYes.title: Fix missing timeouts (ERR-008): set explicit per-call and end-to-end timeouts
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Calls without timeouts can hang forever, exhausting threads/connections and freezing the service.

Find all instances: Search external/blocking operations (HTTP/DB/RPC/queue/subprocess/file) for missing timeouts.

Fix correctly: Set explicit per-call timeouts and an end-to-end deadline; fail fast and clean up on timeout.

Constraints: Config over hardcoding for timeout values. Propagate deadlines (ERR-009).

Acceptance: All external calls have timeouts. Add a test simulating a hang proving the call times out rather than blocking indefinitely.

checks.question: Are top-level timeouts applied that do not propagate into subqueries, retries, streams, locks, or nested calls (timeout applied at wrong layer only)? (ERR-009)

onYes.title: Fix non-propagating timeouts (ERR-009): thread deadlines through the chain
onYes.prompt:
Problem: A top-level timeout that doesn't reach inner calls lets inner operations run past the deadline, leaking work and resources.

Find all instances: Search for outer timeouts/cancellation tokens not passed into nested calls, retries, streams, or lock acquisitions.

Fix correctly: Propagate the cancellation token/deadline through every blocking operation in the call chain.

Constraints: Don't replace or drop the token mid-chain (CON-007).

Acceptance: Deadlines propagate end-to-end. Add a test asserting an outer cancellation aborts inner work promptly.

checks.question: Are high-volume calls to fragile dependencies made without failure isolation (no circuit breaker, bounded pool, or bulkhead)? (ERR-010)

onYes.title: Fix missing circuit breaker/bulkhead (ERR-010): isolate failing dependencies
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Without isolation, a failing dependency can exhaust resources and cascade into a full outage.

Find all instances: Search high-volume calls to fragile dependencies lacking circuit breakers, bounded pools, or bulkheads.

Fix correctly: Add circuit breakers, bounded concurrency/pools, queues, or bulkheads to contain dependency failures.

Constraints: Pair with fallback/degradation (ERR-011). Config over hardcoding for thresholds.

Acceptance: Dependency failures are isolated. Add a test asserting the breaker opens/limits load under sustained failure.

checks.question: Do non-critical dependencies cause total request/service failure when unavailable, lacking a degradation path? (ERR-011)

onYes.title: Fix missing degradation path (ERR-011): degrade gracefully for non-critical deps
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Letting an optional dependency fail the whole request reduces availability unnecessarily.

Find all instances: Search for non-critical dependency calls whose failure aborts the entire operation.

Fix correctly: Provide a fallback, cached data, queueing, or an explicit degraded response when non-critical dependencies are unavailable.

Constraints: Distinguish critical from non-critical correctly; degrade only what is safe.

Acceptance: Non-critical failures degrade gracefully. Add a test asserting the core operation still succeeds when an optional dependency fails.

checks.question: Do reusable libraries call process exit, panic, abort, fatal log, or hard termination instead of returning errors to the host (fatal exit in reusable library)? (ERR-012)

onYes.title: Fix fatal exit in library (ERR-012): return errors, let the host decide
onYes.prompt:
Problem: A library that kills the process removes the host's ability to handle failures gracefully.

Find all instances: Search library/shared code for process exit, abort, panic, or fatal-log calls in non-main paths.

Fix correctly: Return errors (typed results/exceptions) and let the host application decide whether to terminate.

Constraints: Reserve hard exit for application entry points, not libraries.

Acceptance: Libraries surface errors instead of exiting. Add a test asserting an error condition returns an error rather than terminating the process.

checks.question: Are errors represented only as strings, booleans, nulls, magic codes, or generic exceptions, making them hard to handle programmatically (ambiguous error value)? (ERR-013)

onYes.title: Fix ambiguous error values (ERR-013): use typed/structured errors
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Stringly-typed/generic errors can't be reliably matched, leading to fragile handling.

Find all instances: Search for errors signaled via bare strings/booleans/null/magic codes/generic exceptions where callers must branch on them.

Fix correctly: Use typed errors or structured error codes carrying category and context.

Constraints: Keep a consistent error model per boundary (ERR-017).

Acceptance: Errors are typed/structured. Add tests matching on error type/code rather than message text.

checks.question: Do error responses leak internal details (stack traces, SQL, filesystem paths, tokens, config, internal identifiers) to users (internal details leaked in error)? (ERR-014)

onYes.title: Fix internal details in errors (ERR-014): safe messages, private logs
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Detailed error output aids attackers and may leak secrets/PII.

Find all instances: Search error responses for stack traces, SQL, paths, tokens, config, or internal IDs returned to clients.

Fix correctly: Return safe, generic user-facing messages with a correlation ID; log the sensitive details privately. Disable verbose error pages in production.

Constraints: Don't leak secrets (CSP-002). Keep diagnostics in private logs.

Acceptance: Client errors are sanitized; details go to logs. Add a test asserting an internal failure returns a safe message without stack/secret content.

checks.question: Are recoverable and unrecoverable error branches lacking tests (error path untested)? (ERR-015)

onYes.title: Fix untested error paths (ERR-015): add failure-behavior tests
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Untested error paths frequently hide bugs that only appear during incidents.

Find all instances: Search for error branches (cleanup, propagation, fallback, user-visible errors) without tests.

Fix correctly: Add tests covering failure behavior: correct error surfaced, cleanup performed, propagation, and user-visible error shape.

Constraints: Don't weaken behavior to make tests pass; test the real failure handling.

Acceptance: Important error paths are tested. Add tests exercising representative recoverable and unrecoverable failures.

checks.question: Do multi-step writes leave inconsistent state when a later step fails, without compensation (partial write without compensation)? (ERR-016)

onYes.title: Fix partial writes (ERR-016): use transactions or compensation
onYes.prompt:
Problem: A failure after some writes but before others leaves the system inconsistent.

Find all instances: Search multi-step persistence sequences where a later failure leaves earlier writes committed.

Fix correctly: Wrap the change in a transaction, or use rollback/outbox/saga/reconciliation to compensate on failure.

Constraints: For cross-service steps use saga/outbox (CON-014). Make steps idempotent (CON-016).

Acceptance: Partial failures don't leave inconsistent state. Add a test forcing a mid-sequence failure and asserting consistent (rolled-back or compensated) state.

checks.question: Are mixed exception/result/status/null error conventions used within the same boundary or module (inconsistent error model)? (ERR-017)

onYes.title: Fix inconsistent error model (ERR-017): standardize error representation
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Mixed error conventions confuse callers and cause mishandled failures.

Find all instances: Search a module/boundary for mixed conventions (some throw, some return null, some return result/status).

Fix correctly: Standardize on one error representation per boundary and convert consistently at boundaries.

Constraints: Convert at the boundary; keep internal consistency. Preserve cause/context.

Acceptance: Error handling is consistent within the boundary. Add tests verifying the standardized error shape across representative operations.

checks.question: Are promises/tasks/futures/coroutines/goroutines/background jobs launched without awaiting or supervision, so their failures go unobserved (unobserved async failure)? (ERR-018)

onYes.title: Fix unobserved async failures (ERR-018): await or supervise background work
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Fire-and-forget async work can fail silently, losing data and hiding errors.

Find all instances: Search for async work started without await/join/supervision (un-awaited tasks, detached goroutines, fire-and-forget jobs).

Fix correctly: Await, collect results, or supervise async work with error handling/logging and lifecycle ownership.

Constraints: Tie lifecycle to the parent (CON-005/CON-006). Don't swallow the resulting errors (ERR-001).

Acceptance: Async failures are observed. Add a test asserting a failing background task's error is surfaced/logged.

checks.question: Is missing required configuration silently replaced with defaults in production paths, hiding startup misconfiguration (startup failure hidden by fallback config)? (ERR-019)

onYes.title: Fix hidden startup misconfig (ERR-019): fail fast on missing required config
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Silently defaulting required config can run the app in an insecure/incorrect state.

Find all instances: Search startup/config loading for required values that fall back to defaults when absent.

Fix correctly: Validate required configuration at startup and fail fast with a clear error when it is missing/invalid.

Constraints: Distinguish truly-required from optional config. Config over hardcoding (OPS-009).

Acceptance: Missing required config aborts startup. Add a test asserting startup fails clearly when a required value is absent.

checks.question: Do shutdown paths ignore failures when flushing, closing, draining, syncing, or acknowledging work (shutdown errors ignored)? (ERR-020)

onYes.title: Fix ignored shutdown errors (ERR-020): report and handle shutdown failures
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Ignoring shutdown errors loses unflushed data and leaves resources improperly closed.

Find all instances: Search shutdown handlers for ignored failures while flushing buffers, closing connections, draining queues, syncing files, or acking work.

Fix correctly: Report shutdown failures and ensure resources close safely; surface non-clean shutdown to operators.

Constraints: Combine with graceful shutdown (RES-018). Don't swallow errors (ERR-001).

Acceptance: Shutdown failures are handled/reported. Add a test asserting a flush/close failure during shutdown is surfaced rather than ignored.
